# 2 Baruch Chapter 36 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Third Fast and Vision

---

**1** And I lay down and slept, and I saw a vision in the night.

**2** And behold, a forest of trees stood upon a plain, and there were cedars large and lofty, and there were thorns and brambles around them.

**3** And on the other side there was a vine of grapevines, lowly and humble; and from it came a stream of water.

**4** And that vine grew and came to the forest; and in a short time it filled the whole forest, and uprooted all the cedars, and threw down and scattered all that was lofty.

**5** And the head of the cedars that had been thrown down — the vine dried up that head and laid it low on the ground.

**6** And the rest of the cedars lay prostrate, and they fell at the root of the vine that had thrown them down; and not one of them remained.

**7** And that vine grew and became exalted and became lord of the whole forest; and from it the water flowed more abundantly than before, and all the pleasant trees of the earth came to it as a delight to the eye.

**8** And it spread itself over the whole plain, and the whole earth was filled with its fruit.

**9** Then I saw this and I arose.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal equivalence rendering of the cedar-vine vision. The forest = empire; the vine = messianic kingdom. The vine is "lowly and humble" (v.3) — a deliberate contrast with the lofty cedars. The interpretation is given in chs. 39-40.*
